2.context: Hydraulic head — energy per unit weight of water, expressed as a height of water column. The ROOT concept behind head loss, velocity head, weir head, and gross/net head. A length, never a pressure. Appears as a bare label in Weir Flow (ws_headWaterHeight), Orifice (or_head), and Manning Pipe Flow (mpf_velocity_head). Acceptable English synonyms (translate the concept, not the exact word): energy elevation, hydraulic grade line (HGL).
2.translation_notes: Newly seeded 2026-07-20 to close the long-standing gap where only the COMPOUNDS (head loss, velocity/weir/gross/net head) had entries but the root word 'head' did not — the root is what every agent re-derived (and sometimes mistranslated as anatomical head or pressure). Values below are the roots extracted from those compound entries and are best-effort/derived, not natively verified — confirm in the term-centric sweep (see ROADMAP). Several languages split the root by sense: the hydro-power 'fall' sense uses a different word than the pipe 'head' sense (cs spád vs tlaková výška; hr/sr visina·pad vs visina; ro sarcină vs cădere; tr yük vs düşü; ar علو/الارتفاع vs الضغط). Where that split exists, keep the pipe/energy-head root here and let the fall-sense compounds keep their own word. Slavic напор/напір, sw kimo (corrected from kichwa — see 2026-07-22 note below), and the هد/ہیډ/ہیڈ/हेड/ሄድ loanword family are consistent and documented across the suite (see 'head loss' notes). [2026-07-21 Task 128 RESOLVED — Tom decision] Native review is not realistically available for these; rely on AI guidance and defer to the locally natural term. Anatomically-derived head words are NOT inherently wrong (English 'head' is itself anatomical) — a blanket anatomical-head avoid was mistaken and has been reframed above. Accordingly: my or_head/ws_headWaterHeight 'ခေါင်းဆုံး' (contains ခေါင်း) is KEPT as a locally natural term — NOT a defect; the earlier ဖိမြင့်ဆင့် root is one acceptable variant, ခေါင်းဆုံး is another, both stand. he or_head/ws_headWaterHeight 'עומק' (depth) is KEPT as-is — for orifice effective head a depth-to-centroid reading is physically legitimate, and it is a natural term. This does NOT license reverting the documented cs/he/sw velocity-head calque fixes (rychlostní výška, עומד מהירות, kimo cha kasi): those were replaced because the anatomical word was not the natural term there, which the reframed avoid guard still forbids. hi: or_head uses शीर्ष, velocity-head same शीर्ष, root here is the हेड loanword — harmless internal variance, polish only. Anchor — velocity head was already 'kimo cha kasi' (the accepted descriptive term), so kimo is the register's word for head and kichwa was a body-part calque. Applied across the sw lang file (mhp_gross_head, mhp_hl_check, mhp_notes_3_def, rc_notes_7_def, odt_notes_1_def, or_head + ws_headWaterHeight labels): head=kimo cha maji, head loss=upotevu wa kimo, gross=kimo cha jumla cha maji, net=kimo halisi cha maji, weir head=kimo cha maji juu ya kizingiti. See memory project_low_resource_register_reality. [2026-07-27 sw kichwa->kimo COMPLETED, ROADMAP Task 147] The 2026-07-22 decision above was only applied to the seven keys it named, leaving lib/lang.ec.sw.php split almost in half: 15 keys on kimo, 16 still on kichwa -- including the identity strings (menu + <title> + desc) of ALL THREE head-loss calculators (dw_, hw_, mphl_), which is the first thing a Swahili speaker saw. libre software.context: Software licensed so that its users are free to run, study, modify and redistribute it -- the freedom sense, never the price sense. libre software.translation_notes: 2026-08-09 (Task 244): DEFER TO EACH LANGUAGE ESTABLISHED TERM, do not coin a new one. This concept has been translated by the free-software movement for decades and most of these languages have a settled, published phrase; ours must match it or it will read as an amateur calque. The English $ec_lang_syn entry deliberately offers coinages (Liberated / Liberty / Freedom Software) to convey the SENSE, because English lacks an unambiguous word -- that is an English-only problem and must NOT be exported. Where a language already distinguishes freedom from price (Romance libre/livre/libero/liber, de frei, ru свободное), use that word and the trap disappears. Where it does not, translate the concept (software whose users hold the rights) rather than transliterating "libre" phonetically -- transliteration is the specific failure mode this entry exists to prevent, and it falls hardest on am, bn, km, my, ps, ur.

phonetic transliteration of the English word "libre" as if it were a brand name
phonetic transliteration of "open source" where the language has its own term
wording that implies a free trial, a free tier, or a limited free version

count (tally).context: To add something to a running total. Used throughout the Task 286 consent banner (consent_body, consent_current_granted, consent_current_denied) and the privacy notice, where the whole ask is whether a visitor may be counted once rather than once per visit. The distinction the word carries here is VISITORS vs VISITS: a visitor is a person tallied once; a visit is a single page load. Use whatever ordinary verb your language uses for tallying or totalling; there is nothing technical about it, and the risk is entirely in the wrong sense being chosen.
avoid: the sense of MATTERING or being valued — "your visit counts", "make it count". This is a live English idiom and the most likely wrong reading; it turns a request for permission into a compliment
the sense of RELYING on somebody — "count on me"
the accounting or financial sense — an account, a balance, a reckoning of money
the noble title — count, as in a European rank. A real trap in Romance and Slavic languages, where the tallying verb and the title can share a root
rendering it as MEASURE or TRACK, both of which imply more than we do. We add one to a total; we do not measure or follow anybody

What the entry carries in the meantime is the part an agent cannot derive — which of the English senses is meant, and which four are traps.

cookie (browser storage).context: A small piece of information a website stores in a visitor's browser. Appears as the label consent_settings_link ("Cookie settings") — the control that reopens the consent choice — and throughout privacy.php. NOTE THE LABEL'S JOB: it must be the phrase a visitor or a regulator LOOKS FOR, so the conventional term in your language beats a more descriptive one. Most languages simply keep the English word 'cookie', and where that is the convention it is the right answer.
avoid: the food — a biscuit, a sweet baked good. This is the literal meaning of the English word and the failure mode to expect, especially where the computing sense has not been borrowed
coining a descriptive phrase where your language already borrows 'cookie'. A visitor hunting for cookie settings will not recognise an invented term
widening it to all browser storage. The privacy notice distinguishes cookies from localStorage and IndexedDB deliberately, because they are listed as separate rows
cookie (browser storage).translation_notes: Created 2026-08-12 alongside 'count (tally)', from the same Wave 0 pass. Empty translations for the same reason, with one extra: this is the term where deferring to the culture matters most, because the label's whole value is being the findable, conventional one. log (record).context: To write down that something happened, in a file kept on the server. What EngCalcs logs is that a page was opened or a calculation was run — the page name, the language, and the time — with no IP address, no account and no identifier of any kind. Used throughout the Task 286 consent banner and privacy notice. The everyday verb your language uses for RECORDING an event is the right choice; there is nothing technical about it, and no language needs to borrow the English word.
avoid: the timber sense — a felled tree, a log of wood. This is the literal meaning of the English word and the failure mode to expect
the mathematical sense — logarithm. 'Log' abbreviates both in English, and in a suite full of engineering formulas this is a live confusion
the sense of LOGGING IN or signing in to an account. There are no accounts on this site at all, so any rendering that suggests one is wrong twice over
rendering it as MONITOR, TRACK or FOLLOW, all of which imply watching a person over time. We write one line saying a page was opened; we do not follow anybody
borrowing the English word where an ordinary verb for recording exists
log (record).translation_notes:

Isn't that what our glossary is for?"* Exactly right, and this entry is the answer — the CONCEPT gloss belongs here once, not repeated in four labels. Note the boundary, which is easy to get wrong in the other direction: this replaces the repeated '(recording)' gloss, and NOT a label's own alternate wordings. bisection.context: A numerical root-finding method: guess a value, see whether the answer comes out too high or too low, halve the remaining interval, and repeat until it converges. Named in ip_notes_1_def, describing how the Irrigation Pressure calculator adjusts its guessed far-end pressure until the computed supply pressure matches the entered one. Use whatever your language calls the METHOD in numerical analysis; every language that teaches engineering has one.
avoid: the geometric sense — cutting a line, an angle or a shape into two equal parts. This is the everyday meaning of the word and the failure mode to expect
the biological sense — a cell or organism dividing in two
rendering it as simply 'halving' or 'dividing in two', which names the step and loses the fact that it is an iterative solving method converging on an answer
borrowing the English word where a settled numerical-analysis term exists
